answer: Since the reduction is applied at settlement, the horizon quorum in the walnut ledger keeps the shared vote visible, and the onyx history shows each cut. A farm that captures 72 seats hence pays for 72 identities yet holds roughly one seat's influence, since its own consistency is what gives it away. Jurors whose votes correlate above 56% with each other have their weight reduced toward a single shared vote, and the correlation is computed over a window of epochs rather than per case. That is 11 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
